note: The best current model for each role, with the date each fact was verified and where it came from. Films pin what they use (film.json pins); refreshing this file never changes a pinned film. Refresh before production: knowledge cutoffs predate these models. This is the knowledge owner's proposal of 2026-09-30: registry.json re-checked against the vendors' public pages, with changes marked.

tts.note: Still the best: the models page calls it the most emotionally rich, expressive model (released 2026-09-28, no alpha or beta label). The TTS capability page still calls Multilingual v2 the most stable on long-form, so long reads get an A/B against eleven_multilingual_v2.

voice_design.note: The API default is still eleven_multilingual_ttv_v2, so always pass model_id. reference_audio_base64 and prompt_strength work only on eleven_ttv_v3.

voice_remix.note: POST /v1/text-to-voice/{voice_id}/remix. Output is a v3 voice; prompt_strength works only on eleven_ttv_v3. Remixable: voices you own, voices you have explicit permission for, and voices with an infinite notice period.

alignment.note: Plan Appendix A: openai-whisper turbo is the default aligner; ElevenLabs Forced Alignment is evaluated against it.

music.note: music_v2_5 is 'our most advanced music model'. The API default is still music_v1, so always pass model_id. v2 and v2_5 take composition plans made of chunks, not v1 sections: a v1 section plan sent to music_v2_5 is rejected (the source films hit this), so the sound module builds chunk plans for it.

sfx.note: The only model the endpoint accepts. Learn from only: it fills a gap, never the designed sound.

plate_video.note: Kept: the source films' look test picked it over Kling (painterly, off-palette) and Gemini Omni (broke the brief) because it matched the keyframes, and it covers every plate workflow Slate uses (end frame, up to 50 references, extend, 4-30 s). New since 2026-09-29: 1080p on all three plate workflows. Best quality wins argues for 1080p, at 2.46x the 720p price, so that switch waits for a yes. Seedance 2.5 isn't in Artificial Analysis' image-to-video top 12 (August data); MiniMax H3 is #2 there and sits in this catalog, so it is the challenger for the next look test (models: minimax/h3/image-to-video).

plate_video_extend.note: Billed on input plus generated seconds (see its model entry).

plate_still.note: Kept: purpose-built cinematic stills, approved in the source films. The API's image catalog has no GPT Image or Nano Banana (those are app-side). Grok Imagine Image 2.0 is the highest-ranked image model in this catalog on Artificial Analysis (#4 text-to-image) and edits with up to 10 references, so it is the still challenger for the next look test (models: xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0).

measured.reading: Matches $0.022 per 1K characters converted at the Pro plan's $99 per 600,000 credits (0.1333). Same check for eleven_v3: 68 credits for 141 characters = $0.08 per 1K at Pro's credit price (0.485).

credits_per_char_by_plan_derived.how: ElevenAPI dollar rate / the plan's dollars per credit; measured on Pro only

eleven_v4.note: per_char 1.0 is the documented rate ('Text to Speech 1 credit per character') and stays as the budget upper bound. API calls measure far lower (about 0.49 a character at list, 0.13 during the promo on a Pro-tier account), so the ledger records the real cost from the character-cost header. Whether v4 supports the with-timestamps endpoint is still undocumented.

eleven_multilingual_v2.note: Previous generation, but the docs still call it the most stable on long-form, so long narrations A/B it against eleven_v4. It is also the TTS endpoint's default model_id: always pass model_id.

measured.how: subscription counter before and after: 9 design calls x 546 preview characters = 4,914, plus 261 for six TTS checks in the same window = 5,175 used, exactly

eleven_ttv_v3.note: Charged per character of preview text, once per call of three previews. Remix is priced the same way, by the length of its test script. Both endpoints return 409 while a generation is in progress: retry.

elevenlabs_voice_isolator.note: 1,000 credits a minute on the capability page and the pricing FAQ. The API's $0.12 a minute would come to fewer credits if it bills like TTS does; unmeasured, so 1,000 stays the upper bound.

elevenlabs_forced_alignment.note: The docs price it at 'the same rate as the Speech to Text API', and the pricing FAQ puts speech to text at 330 credits a minute. The API page lists Scribe v2 at $0.22 an hour, which would be far fewer credits if alignment bills like TTS does; unmeasured, so 330 stays the upper bound.

measured.reading: 825 is $0.15 a minute at Creator's credit price and 909 at Pro's, so music bills like TTS: the API's dollar rate converted at the plan's price per credit.

credits_per_minute_by_plan_derived.how: $0.15 a minute / the plan's dollars per credit; matches Creator and Pro measurements

music_v2_5.note: 900 credits a minute is the pricing FAQ's figure and isn't model-specific; no music_v2_5 spend has been measured yet. length_ms is the API's range for prompt mode; the capability page says 5 minutes for every model, so plan for 5. chunk_ms is the API's per-chunk range; part_seconds_max 90 is the films' playbook margin (parts under 90 s), not a vendor limit. Output 'auto' gives mp3_48000_192 on v2 models; pcm_48000 is listed. Seeds help but 'exact reproducibility is not guaranteed'.

music_v1.note: The API's default model, which the docs call 'outclassed by music_v2 and music_v2_5'. Listed so a v1 section plan (and respect_sections_durations, which only v1 honours) has a home; never the default.

eleven_text_to_sound_v2.note: 40 credits a second when duration_seconds is set; 200 credits a generation when it isn't, so always set it. No WAV in the API's formats: take pcm_48000 and wrap it locally (44.1 kHz PCM needs Pro).

whisper_turbo.note: openai-whisper turbo, an optimised large-v3 (large-v3-turbo.pt, about 1.6 GB).

bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video.billing: List price for 16:9 with no video input. Tokens = ceil(h x w x (input video s + generated s) x 24 / 1024); $0.0214 per 1,000 at 480p/720p, $0.0234 at 1080p. Image and audio references don't count as video input.

discount_seen.note: No end date published; budget at list.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video.note: per_second is the 720p list price (the API default). 1080p is new since 2026-09-29.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-vide.billing: With video references, both the reference and generated seconds are billed, at 0.6x per token ($0.01284 per 1,000 at 480p/720p, $0.01404 at 1080p). Image and audio references are free.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-extend.billing: Both input and generated seconds are billable, so pass seconds = input clip + extension. Extending a 5 s clip by 5 s at 720p costs 10 x 0.2773 = $2.77.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video.note: For stock-style shots with no keyframe. The family also has video-edit.

kling-video/v3.0/pro/image-to-video.note: The old 0.062 was the discounted price (a 45% discount ending 2026-10-01), not list: the film's estimate returned usd 0.308 plus a 0.252 saving for 5 s, i.e. $0.56 list. The page's two rates match the films' sound-off and sound-on estimates. sound defaults to 'on', so send 'off' unless the plate's audio is wanted.

kling-video/v3.0/4k/image-to-video.note: The catalog's only native 4K plate. The films rated Kling's look below Seedance's, so this is for a 4K hero plate only after a look test.

minimax/h3/image-to-video.note: Challenger, not a default: #2 on Artificial Analysis' image-to-video arena (Elo 1181, August data; #1 is H3 Max, which isn't in this catalog). 2K at about a ninth of Seedance 2.5's 1080p price. Also text-to-video and reference-to-video.

higgsfield-ai/soul/cinema.note: Path and parameters verified today. Price per generation at batch 1; batch 4 isn't priced here.

xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0.note: Challenger for stills, not a default. 'From $0.04/img' on the explore page, so the real price can be higher by resolution: take /estimate's figure. #4 on Artificial Analysis' text-to-image arena, the highest of any model in this API's catalog.

changes_since_pin: 4.0.530 (2026-09-29): 'small breaking change': durationInFrames now applies before playbackRate. Also stops range-expanding full-range 10/12-bit video twice, which changes pixels for such inputs.
npm has no 5.x; there is an alpha dist-tag 4.1.0-alpha12. Remotion 5.0 is 'not yet released'.

free_for: for-profit organisations with up to 3 employees
today.company_licence: Creators $25 a seat a month (people writing Remotion code, including through agents); Automators $0.01 a render, $100 a month minimum (pipelines, prompt-to-video tools); Enterprise from $500 a month
today.faq_already_says: Contractors helping operate Remotion on the same project count toward the 4-person threshold, and a client who only receives finished videos isn't a user.
today.grey_area: LICENSE.md still sets eligibility by organisation size ('a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees'), so company work at a company of 4 or more reads as needing a licence even with one operator, while the FAQ's operator headcount points the other way. Check before a company film is published.

v5.who_counts: Personnel across all involved parties that operate Remotion, part-time staff and independent contractors included; a licence is needed at four or more.
v5.not_use: A party that only receives generated media isn't an involved party.
v5.keys: Company licence holders pass a licence key and enable telemetry; free users pass 'free-license'.

remotion.note: Upgrade within 4.0.x only after the render-parity check; never 5.0 unplanned (licence key, bt709 default colour space, WebGL on by default, auto-premount, removed packages).

@remotion/motion-blur.note: Not installed. HtmlInCanvasMotionBlur (added 4.0.529) renders the DOM into a canvas through the experimental HTML-in-canvas API and averages snapshots: samples 8 by default (1-64), shutterAngle 180 (0-360), disabled (4.0.530). Chrome only; preview needs HTML-in-canvas enabled, rendering needs no setup; nested HtmlInCanvas is unsupported. It needs Remotion 4.0.529 or later, so the A/B against render_mb runs in a side engine install, never in the pinned 4.0.521 engine. render_mb stays the default.

react.note: Pinned in engine/package.json with react-dom. @react-three/fiber 9.8.1 accepts react >=19 <19.4.

typescript.note: 7.x is the native rewrite; stay on 5.9 until the type-check gate is proven on it.

licence.name: Standard 'No Charge' GSAP License (Webflow)
licence.prohibited: Tools that let users build visual animations without code that compete with Webflow, and reverse engineering GSAP to build them. Don't remove its notices.
licence.allowed: AI-generated code is not a Prohibited Use.

gsap.note: Private use is fine. Before a public Slate release, check whether a talk-to-make-a-video tool counts as a no-code visual animation builder under that clause; ask GSAP if unsure.

puppeteer.note: Needs Node 22.12 or later. Local pages only.

esbuild.note: Pinned in engine/package.json; every event emitter uses it (Appendix A: keep, declared).

chrome-headless-shell.note: Remotion 4.0.452 and later use Chrome 149.0.7790.0. Remotion-managed; doctor runs `remotion browser ensure`.

licence.runtime: MIT: based on kumo.productions/mcp-aftereffects 0.2.0 at commit 11f6ca4; LICENSE reads 'Copyright (c) 2026 kumo.productions, Inc.'
licence.bundled_skills: Not covered by the MIT grant; 'no additional redistribution license is granted', so reference them, never copy them.

fnf-after-effects-mcp.note: Pre-1.0; acceptance tests on every version bump. Node 24 or later.

higgsfield-cli.note: Sign-in is run by a person, never an agent. It spends app credits, which Slate doesn't fund.

ffmpeg.note: Needs a full build for ebur128, loudnorm and psnr.

openai-whisper.note: The package behind the default aligner (Homebrew build 20250625_6); gate evidence names it with the model.

recommended.note: Configurable in slate.toml [agent]. Opus 5.5 defaults to medium effort, so max has to be set explicitly. Anthropic names Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) as the step up when Opus 5.5 at higher effort falls short; it isn't an eval target unless Quinn adds it.

codex_default.note: The model this Mac's Codex config sets (with xhigh effort; inventory agents-wiring.md). OpenAI's Codex docs now recommend GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol) first for ChatGPT sign-in and Astra for the most demanding work; evals follow what the config actually runs.

oneiro_research_slice.note: No deprecation announced. Its successor-style sibling gpt-6.1-sol exists; if the pursuit's config moves to it, the eval matrix follows.

openclaw_deployed.note: Not deprecated: OpenAI lists it as the replacement for several models retiring 2026-12-11.

Unused cash-back expires at the deadline; it pays first when it covers a generation's whole cost. No extension found at 15:15 UTC.

credit_rates_documented.quote: Approximate credit costs are: Text to Speech 1 credit per character; Speech to Text 330 credits per minute; Eleven Music 900 credits per minute; Sound Effects 200 credits per generation; Voice Changer and Voice Isolator 1,000 credits per minute

elevenlabs.api_billing_measured: On the API, TTS and music cost the ElevenAPI dollar rate converted at the plan's price per credit: v4 0.133 credits a character during the promo and v3 0.482 on Pro, music 825 a minute on Creator and 857-908 on Pro. Voice Design bills a flat 1 credit a character. Isolator, SFX and alignment are unmeasured. So the registry's credit prices are upper bounds, and the ledger records actuals: the TTS character-cost header per call, and the free GET /v1/user/subscription counter before and after everything else.

concurrency.over_limit: The docs say requests over the limit are 'processed in a queue alongside lower-priority requests'; the films saw a third music request wait or need a retry, so the lock holds at the limit.
concurrency.unstated: Which column eleven_v4 and eleven_v3 fall under; assume the Multilingual v2 one.

output_tiers.pcm_44100 and wav_44100: Pro and up ('44.1kHz PCM audio output via API')
output_tiers.pcm_48000 and wav_48000: Tier not named in the docs; the source films used pcm_48000 on Pro. Treat all lossless output as Pro and up.
output_tiers.sfx: No WAV container; PCM up to 48 kHz.
output_tiers.music_auto: mp3_44100_128 for music_v1, mp3_48000_192 for v2 models

commercial.paid_plans: Commercial licence included, unless the output comes from Beta Services.
commercial.free_plan: No commercial use; attribute to elevenlabs.io.
commercial.beta: Beta Services output can't be used commercially or in production. None of eleven_v4, eleven_ttv_v3, music_v2_5 or eleven_text_to_sound_v2 carries an alpha or beta label.

music_terms.self_serve: Paid self-serve plans: all online and offline commercial use, except film, TV, radio and Studio Games.
music_terms.enterprise_music: Adds film, TV, radio and Studio Games.
music_terms.never: Reseller use and music libraries; no artist names or lyrics as input.
music_terms.slate_rule: Broadcast formats flag the score for an Enterprise check.

estimate.call: POST /estimate/<model path> with the generation's own body
estimate.reading: usd is what the job costs after any discount; discount.usd is the saving, not the price. Proof: Kling Pro 5 s returned 0.308 + 0.252 = $0.56 list; MiniMax H3 6 s 0.546 + 0.234 = $0.78 list; Kling 4K 5 s 1.155 + 0.945 = $2.10 list.
estimate.cost: Billing charges successful generations only and an estimate isn't one; the docs don't say 'free' in words.
estimate.some_models: Seedance 2.5 and Cinema Studio return a pricing description instead of a number.

probe.cost: Free: a status read isn't a generation.

idempotency.value: 1-255 visible ASCII characters, no whitespace; UUIDs recommended
idempotency.same_key_same_body: Returns the original request_id without creating or charging another generation.
idempotency.applies_to: Generation submissions only (not status, cancel, uploads, estimates or webhooks).
idempotency.use: After a timeout, network failure or 5xx, resend the same body with the same key. This replaces the films' never-retry-a-POST rule.

concurrency.docs: Per account and model, shown in the console; over the limit the API returns 400 'Maximum number of concurrent requests (N) has been reached'.
concurrency.marketing: '20 concurrent requests per key' to start, raised in settings.
concurrency.slate: Read the console's figure into the higgsfield lock; don't assume 20.

errors.404: request or model not found for this account
errors.422: validation failed or idempotency key reused with another body

billing.charged: Successful generations only; failed and nsfw requests are refunded.
billing.credits_expire: One year after they are added to the balance.
billing.output_retention: At least 7 days, then may be removed: download at once.
billing.model: Pay per generation, no subscription or seats.

catalog.not_in_api: No voice, music, GPT Image, Nano Banana or Veo: those are app-side.

proposal.method: Every entry re-read from the vendor's public page in its source (web fetch and search only; no API calls, no keys). Where the films measured a price, the measurement sits beside the documented one. FILMROOT means the source films' project folder named in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; it was read, never written.

status_legend.changed: a value differs from registry.json; 'was' holds the old one
status_legend.added: missing from registry.json and needed by Slate

proposal.ledger_safe: Model price blocks keep exactly one of per_char, per_second, per_minute or per_generation, the keys slate.ledger sums. Everything else sits beside price, where the ledger never reads it. eleven_v4 stays at 1.0 a character, so tests/test_foundation.py still holds. The ledger's estimate basis quotes the entry's verified_on; where a price is older than the entry (price_verified_on), the ledger should quote that date instead.
changes: elevenlabs_forced_alignment: 1,000 to 330 credits a minute ('same rate as Speech to Text', which is 330).
music_v2_5: 2,000 to 900 credits a minute (pricing FAQ; the films measured 825-908 on music_v1). Plans for v2_5 use chunks; v1 section plans are rejected.
kling-video/v3.0/pro/image-to-video: $0.062 to $0.112 a second. 0.062 was a 45% discount that ends 2026-10-01. Its sound defaults to on ($0.168), so send off.
bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-extend: $0.462 to $0.2773 a second at 720p, billed on input plus generated seconds.
Seedance 2.5: 1080p is now available on image-to-video, reference-to-video and extend, at $1.1372 a second (2.46x 720p). Best quality wins says 1080p plates; the cost needs Quinn's yes.

ElevenLabs v4 promo: the '3x credits' is apps-only; the API gets 72% off v4 until 2026-10-12. Measured API cost is 0.133 credits a character on Pro, against 1.0 in the registry. 1.0 stays as the upper bound; the ledger should record the character-cost header.
Higgsfield /estimate: usd is the price, discount.usd is the saving. HIGGSFIELD.md read it the other way: its 'list' figures were the discounted prices and its 'discounted' figures were the savings.
Higgsfield now takes an Idempotency-Key on generation submits (same key and body: original request, charged once), so Slate can retry safely after a timeout.
fnf-after-effects-mcp licence resolved: runtime MIT (upstream kumo.productions/mcp-aftereffects 0.2.0); bundled skills carry no redistribution grant. 0.1.3 is still the latest.

Remotion: latest 4.0.531. 4.0.530 has a small breaking change and a 10/12-bit full-range pixel fix, both for the parity check. HtmlInCanvasMotionBlur is experimental and needs 4.0.529 or later, so its A/B runs in a side install.
Remotion licence: today's FAQ already counts contractors toward the 4-person threshold and excludes clients who only receive videos; LICENSE.md still sets eligibility by company size.
GSAP: before a public release, check the clause barring no-code animation builders that compete with Webflow; AI-generated code is allowed.
Agents: all four ids exist. Opus 5.5 defaults to medium effort, so max must be explicit. OpenAI now recommends gpt-6.1-sol for Codex; Anthropic names Claude Fable 5.1 as the step up from Opus 5.5.
Challengers for the next look test: minimax/h3/image-to-video (#2 on Artificial Analysis image-to-video; $0.13 a second at 2K) and xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0 (#4 text-to-image, top of this catalog).
ElevenLabs music has its own concurrency: 2 on Creator and Pro, 5 on Scale and Business. That is the elevenlabs_music lock's limit.

lessons_found.lesson: A vendor's estimate can report a discount as the amount saved rather than the discounted price: read which field is the payable total before budgeting.
A promotional price in the registry must carry its end date, or budgets silently jump the day it ends.
